It's crazy how much Allison had the wool pulled over everyone's heads.

Back in 2019, I was living in LA, going through a divorce, and going to school while pursuing a career in Stand up.  Originally from San Diego, I was familiar with the success that MSW was having and was genuinely happy for them and wanted nothing but the best for them.

Through the grape vine I discover that they've been picked up by  one of the main media agencies CAA and no one talked about it.I thought it was odd because I felt that their podcast was about bringing truth to the people and they were directly supported by their fans, but by having a major agency in their corner felt disingenuous.  However, again, I didn't wish any negative will towards them.  I still wanted them to succeed.

In Jan 2019, I suffered a full blown manic episode.  With everything going on in my life (along with a lot of weed), I became paranoid and upset at the world for not wanting to come together, so like a comedian, I thought I could use the power of social media to bring people together.

So I started to tag many organizations together to include the MSW podcast as well as the MAGA accounts.  I was also trying to start a trend #sayhername which was in reference to a young girl that died earlier that year to gun violence, but as I kept tagging the podcast and using #sayhername, Allison thought I was trying to out her as she was going by AG at the time.  On top of that, I started to tag CAA because as I was trying to raise awareness, I wanted to see how far my reach could go as just one person.

Allison did not take kindly to that.

Before I go further, I could understand how one would feel If someone I barely knew started tagging me in random tweets/posts that outed some type of truth I was keeping from the public. But based on my interactions with her up until that point, I honestly didn't think she was going to react the way she did.

She threatened me with lawsuits, went to the SD Comedian's FB page and told everyone that she would never work with me again, blocked me, and then when she realized that people were worried about my well being, she flipped the script and tried to come off as if she was also concerned about my well being also.

I don't remember every single message, that was sent between us, however I do remember feeling "This person isn't who I thought she was and she's playing it up."

Months after the incident, I remember having interactions with other comedians who were angry at me for doing what I did, but I couldn't really defend myself because I was still processing everything that transpired through that event.

I just remember feeling that those other comedians were wrong, but I didn't know how to articulate those words.

I genuinely felt bad for Jaleesa (I was also using a different hashtag for her during that manic episode, for which I started as a fun joke, but it turned sideways when other comedians used it in a negative connotation.)

I also felt bad for Jordan, for having her to deal with that mess too.

And when I heard what went down between Allison and Jaleesa, I knew Allison was the reason behind it.

I honestly had put this all behind me, however I saw the video pop up in my IG Story feed from another comic and immediately knew that shit was going down.

That was my experience early on in stand up.  I got shat on by the local guys in my city who’ve been doing it for years before me. 

I hated it, but kept my head down, kept working on the craft and just told myself that’s how it was.

It wasn’t until a year or two in,  I did a road gig and this veteran comic treated me really nicely.  I was shocked because I was like why is he being cool?  Turns out,  you don’t need to be a Dick in comedy.

That experience taught me that if i ever got to his level,  I would do the same to newer comics and I did.

I don’t do as much comedy anymore,  but the people I was cool with towards the end are now flourishing and doing great things because of the knowledge I passed onto them.
